features.name: Model selector
features.purpose: Pick which Claude model a session or workflow step runs with, shown with a one-line description per option.
businessRules: description is optional on ModelOption; missing description renders label-only

a step/session keeps a retired model id in storage (no migration); resolveModelId() substitutes the mapped replacement at query time so it still runs, and a warning badge on the step card flags it for the user to update
an unmapped unknown model id passes through resolveModelId() unchanged rather than being forced to a default
architecturalRules: all model Selects must use modelSelectData()/renderModelOption instead of inlining data mapping
modelSelectData() takes the current stored id as ensureId so a stale/unknown id renders disabled instead of leaving the Select blank
legacy-model resolution is a static explicit map (LEGACY_MODEL_MAP), not a tier-prefix heuristic or live Models-API lookup

features.name: Permissions and plan mode
features.purpose: What decides whether a tool call runs, who decided it, and how plan mode's deliverable is written and reviewed: mode pickers, resolution provenance, the synced auto-mode allowlist, plan-file auto-approval, the reopenable plan card, and a typed reply counting as "keep planning".
businessRules: all five PermissionMode values stay selectable, including acceptEdits, because preset workflows ship steps with permissionMode: 'acceptEdits'
'default' displays as Manual; the stored value is unchanged
ExitPlanMode and AskUserQuestion always resolve to an explicit 'ask' from the hook, in every permission mode, never a bare continue: true a mode or settings entry could pre-empt
a second answer to an already-resolved permission request is dropped; it never re-emits a resolution event or re-triggers recoverOrphanedPermission's injected prompt

a resend after a bridge restart replays a stored ALWAYS_ASK_TOOLS resolution only when it was produced by a human (resolvedBy is 'user', 'plan-reply', or absent/legacy); any server-synthesized resolution is re-asked instead
a model-initiated EnterPlanMode sets meta.permissionMode = 'plan' immediately, so a subsequent worker/bridge restart resumes still gated
every resolution logs one [permission] line (session, tool, allow/deny, source)
a remote allowlist is never applied automatically; divergence is shown as an explicit added/removed diff the user accepts or rejects
divergence is detected as a set difference between local and remote entries, never by comparing updatedAt
pushing the local list to storage is suppressed while a review is pending
rejecting a review keeps the local list, pushes it back over the remote row, and is remembered by the remote's content so the same proposal is never re-asked
ALWAYS_ASK_TOOLS (AskUserQuestion, ExitPlanMode) can never be allowlisted
a hand-typed Bash prefix is whitespace-collapsed and may not contain &, &&, ||, ;, or |
non-Bash entries never carry a prefix; one given is silently dropped rather than rejected
plan-directory reads and writes (~/.claude/plans/** or <cwd>/.claude/plans/**) auto-approve in every permission mode
ExitPlanMode and AskUserQuestion always still prompt the user regardless of target path
credential paths (~/.ssh, ~/.aws, .env) always escalate even if nested under a plans directory
any other out-of-cwd file access is unaffected and still escalates

/file (and by extension /tree/find) can read any plan directory reachable from isPlanPath, not just the requesting session's own plan file — a deliberate widening of a route previously confined to project/session roots, scoped to plan directories only
a resolved plan card renders collapsed by default but is always reopenable via its header
action buttons never render once a request is resolved, in the inline card or the fullscreen modal
fullscreen focus mode opens read-only for a resolved plan
when the harness passes no inline plan argument, the card falls back to the turn's last plan-file write, reconstructing Edit-revised plans from the file snapshot
a plan card is live (chevron + Focus enabled) whenever a plan path is known, even with no resolvable inline/snapshot text
opening a plan card re-reads its plan file from disk, so the card (pending or resolved) always shows the plan's current text, not a frozen snapshot
a resolved card whose live text differs from what was captured shows an 'updated since approval' hint

a typed composer reply while an ExitPlanMode card is pending is treated as "keep planning": it denies that one request with the user's text as the reason, unblocking the query instead of queueing behind a promise nothing can resolve; it only fires for a pending ExitPlanMode, never another tool

no attachments: the deny reason is KEEP_PLANNING_MESSAGE plus the user's raw text and nothing else is queued; with attachments: the reason is a note only and the real text/attachments are queued as the next turn once the deny settles the busy query
the plan card's badge shows 'kept planning' (not 'denied') for a denied ExitPlanMode request
architecturalRules: single shared PERMISSION_MODES list — no component defines its own label/description array
SegmentedControl has no per-segment tooltip prop, so per-item tooltips wrap each segment's label in a Tooltip-wrapped full-width span
resolvedBy is optional and every reader treats a missing value as 'user'
findPermissionResolution scans backwards (newest wins), matching the existing convention in exitPlanRequestId
the workflow plan-step gate's recorded resolution: 'allow' was already not a record of the SDK's tool result; resolvedBy: 'workflow-advance' makes that legible rather than changing it
validators live in shared/types.ts so the web client runs the exact same rules as the bridge before sending an entry
allowlist edits are dedicated addGuardAllow/removeGuardAllow/reviewGuardAllowlist intent messages, not folded into the whole-blob UserUiSettings save
the web store never caches the allowlist in localStorage; it is server-authoritative and arrives on every hello
removing an entry has no confirmation modal since it only narrows the guard and fails safe
the review modal is mounted at the app root, not inside Settings, so a divergence reaches the user without requiring a gear click

assessToolCall's self-worker-source check (isSelfWorkerSource) runs before the blanket tool allowlist short-circuit — the first guard verdict an allowlist entry cannot disarm; keep it ordered first in any refactor
isPlanPath resolves the path and anchors containment checks to real directories, not a substring match on the plan-dir marker, so path traversal cannot pass as a plan path
isInside does not resolve symlinks; a symlink planted inside a plan directory pointing elsewhere is accepted as a pre-existing limitation
auto-approved plan writes remain visible as tool_use blocks in the transcript, but the auto-approval permission event is filtered from the UI like other auto-approved calls
PLAN_DIR_MARKER/isPlanFilePath live in shared/types.ts, not autoGuard.ts, so the web client can reuse the same plan-path hint without importing server code

resolveWorkspacePath/workspaceRoots/resolveWorkspaceParam live in server/src/workspacePaths.ts, not server/src/index.ts, so they're importable by their own test — index.ts starts listening as a side effect of being imported

~/.claude/plans is per-OS-user, not per-app-user: under AUTH_ENABLED every signed-in app user on the same machine shares that directory, so this exception can cross app-user boundaries — accepted for now

the plan-file fallback builds data.input.plan/planPath from the transcript alone; the rendered card layers a live filesystem read (useFileContent against /file) on top whenever it's open, falling back to the transcript-only text before that fetch resolves or on failure
the plan-file write is tracked turn-scoped (lastPlanWrite) for text stitching, with a non-reset session-wide fallback (sessionPlanWrite) only consulted when the turn-scoped write is absent
expanded (inline collapse) and focus (fullscreen) are independent state; an effect keyed only on resolution forces both closed once a request resolves
the card's live read means a resolved card can show text the user never approved; the 'updated since approval' hint is the mitigation, not a faithful-approval guarantee

the plan-reply path picks the request id via a single backwards scan (same shape as findPermissionRequest/findPermissionResolution), never a bulk deny-everything-pending pass, so a concurrent unrelated permission card is never touched

the no-attachments plan-reply path never emits a 'user' transcript event or calls prompt() directly — both would open a new turn boundary and corrupt turn-scoped bookkeeping (collectTurns, permissionWaitMs)

features.name: Usage and cost
features.purpose: Plan-usage chip, spend split by model, per-session cost/token/duration in the sidebar, and per-step spend in the workflow stepper — all fed by one accumulate-on-result pass.
businessRules: no login, no chip - enforced server-side (poller never fetches, logout nulls snapshot) and client-side (auth.loggedIn gate)
{type: 'usage', usage: null} means auth is gone (logout or revoked/expired OAuth session), nothing else
a stale snapshot survives transient fetch failures; staleness is shown via 'Updated Xm ago', never by hiding the chip
hello may carry usage: null before the poller's first fetch completes (e.g. after a server restart); a logged-in client keeps its previously held snapshot instead of clearing it
rows keyed by resolveModelId(meta.model), so a retired stored model id folds into its replacement's row
helper-query spend (autoName, summarizeTurn, step-output consolidation) is excluded — the table is chat-turn spend only, not full account spend
costByModel is additive and never backfilled; existing sessions show nothing until their next turn settles
the global rollup is derived client-side from the sessions the store already holds, so deleting a session removes its spend
a result carrying neither cost nor usage opens no row
cost rendered as $X.XX, hidden when totalCostUsd is unset
token icon/tooltip hidden when totalTokens is unset
date rendered en-GB (dd/mm/yyyy) instead of browser-default locale
hovering a badge-state row swaps the status badge for date/cost/tokens meta; row min-height is fixed to prevent layout jump
duration rendered via formatDuration, hidden when totalDurationMs is unset; excludes idle wait between turns and permission-prompt approval wait within a turn
cost rendered as $X.XX next to the step name, hidden when that step's accumulated cost is zero or unset
token icon with a tooltip ('N tokens spent') shown next to the cost label, hidden when that step's accumulated tokens are zero or unset
retries and auto-advance turns on the same step add onto the same array slot rather than overwriting it, for both cost and tokens
duration shown next to the token icon via formatDuration, hidden when that step's accumulated duration is zero or unset; excludes permission-prompt approval wait within the turn
architecturalRules: reuses the existing accumulate-on-result pass in server/src/sessions.ts that already owns totalCostUsd/totalTokens, instead of a new tracking mechanism
no new persistence and no new ws message — costByModel travels inside the existing SessionMeta blob
totalTokens and totalDurationMs accumulate on the SDK result message the same way totalCostUsd already does, rather than introducing a separate tracking mechanism
duration is sourced from the SDK result event's duration_ms, not clock math against turnStartedAt, so it excludes idle time by construction

permission-wait time is deducted via LiveState.permissionWaitMs (measured from askPermission call to resolution) rather than switching to the SDK's duration_api_ms, which would also strip genuine tool-execution time
reuses the existing per-turn SessionMeta.lastCostUsd accumulation instead of adding a new cost-tracking path
tokens mirror the same pattern via a new SessionMeta.lastTokens field rather than a separate tracking mechanism
permission-wait time is deducted via LiveState.permissionWaitMs rather than the SDK's duration_api_ms, which would also strip genuine tool-execution time

features.name: Workflow step versioning
features.purpose: Shared diff-popover UI for warning that a pinned step is stale and for browsing, re-pinning, or restoring any past step version, plus the rules deciding which workflow the editor draft reflects.
businessRules: newest-first, gap-tolerant version list
own steps show full history; foreign steps show published versions only, with the exact pinned version always unioned in
pin/restore is disabled for the currently active version
workflow re-pin changes only which immutable version a ref points to; step-library restore creates a brand-new head version with old content — history is never rewritten
both popovers fetch history on open, not on mount, and re-fetch on every reopen
diff list scrolls independently (ScrollArea.Autosize, mah 280) once it exceeds popover height, so the Update button stays reachable regardless of diff length
Update all re-pins every outdated ref step directly, skipping the per-field diff review
a workflows/sharedWorkflows length change while the modal is already open with a live draft must not re-trigger the pick-a-workflow fallback
loadFrom collapses every step of the loaded workflow by default; a step opens only via explicit selection
architecturalRules: immutable step versions are never deleted or edited, on disk or in storage — only the head list and published flag change
the storage route enforces the foreign-publish filter server-side; client-side version union never bypasses it

init effect tracks the open transition via a prevOpened ref and skips its workflows[0] fallback whenever a draft already exists and this isn't the open transition, to avoid racing the id-reconciliation effect after a new-workflow save
new-workflow id reconciliation matches by name plus deep step equality, not step count alone

features.name: Workflow step lifecycle
features.purpose: How a running workflow step's turn settles into advance, park, or stall; the manual escape hatches for a stuck or stalled step; the bounded consolidation of a step's output before it is handed on; and the sidebar checkmark for a fully-finished workflow.
businessRules: plain Stop during a running workflow step always parks it at waiting-approval; it never advances
a user prompt sent after a force-advance but before the interrupted turn settles clears the 'interrupted' flag and its step stamp
step output hand-off after a force-advance goes through the same (now-bounded) consolidation as a normal advance
a step configured with autoAdvance: true still parks after Stop — Stop overrides the step's own configuration
a plan-approval advance already pending when Stop is pressed is discarded, not delayed: both the flag and its step stamp are cleared
a failed turn (is_error result or a crashed query) also never autoAdvances — it parks the step with stepFailure: 'turn' instead, keeping the error status alive for Retry
the affordance only ever targets the workflow's current step; other steps show no hover state
confirmation copy differs by state: a running step warns its turn is stopped and the last-said text becomes the output; the last step's copy says the workflow finishes
one click on Mark as completed always ends with the workflow on the next step (or done), via a normal settle or the watchdog
each affordance only ever targets the workflow current step, and only while it is genuinely stalled
starting a stalled pending step runs it exactly as a normal advance would — same fresh-start behavior, same hand-off
resuming a stalled done step re-runs its consolidation, so the outputs entry the dead advance never published is filled in first
resuming needs no confirmation dialog — the step is already done, so nothing is being overridden
the last step reading done is a finished workflow, never a stall; it gets no affordance
the Approve button shows a loader and is disabled for the entire consolidation window, not just until the next step's status arrives
the button is also disabled while disconnected, since a dropped WS message would otherwise leave the click looking like it did nothing
the card's copy switches to an in-progress message while advancing
the consolidation window is bounded, so even a hung query or token refresh cannot hold advancing open forever
consolidation only fires when a step ran more than one turn; single-turn steps incur no extra query or latency
on query failure, empty result, or a timeout (consolidateTimeoutMs), falls back to lastAssistantText (per-step-scoped) rather than blocking the workflow
an empty consolidated output is never published, so it cannot overwrite a previously captured value
consolidation is scoped to the stepIndex that just finished, not merely the newest started marker

a step whose template references an {outputs.<name>} that is absent or blank parks at waiting-approval via failTurn (stepFailure: 'pre-run') with a marker naming the missing outputs, instead of running with a silently blank substitution
a step deliverable captured during plan mode comes from the ExitPlanMode plan (inline argument or written plan file), not the turn's trailing chat text
outputs are strictly per-session (WorkflowState.outputs); there is no cross-session write path
prompt tokens are honoured only where the step author wrote them: a token occurring inside substituted content (a step output, the diff, the task text) stays literal instead of being re-expanded
the working-tree diff handed to a fresh-start step is capped with a truncation marker (MAX_DIFF_CHARS) so a large dirty tree degrades the hand-off rather than failing the turn

a plan revised by Edit after the deliverable-producing Write still contributes its current on-disk text to the hand-off, via collectTurns reading the plan file (gated by isPlanPath) instead of the last captured Write content
icon precedence: session.completed -> outline check, status running -> Loader, status.actionable -> pulsing dot, isWorkflowFinished -> filled check, otherwise plain dot
actionable states always win over the finished checkmark so a session needing the user is never masked as done
force-advance (mark last running step completed) also sets the last step done, so a force-finished workflow shows the filled check too

clicking a step in the stepper still jumps the transcript to that step's start marker, but the marker may not be mounted (Transcript.tsx windows a long transcript to its tail): the click asks revealWorkflowStep() to scroll directly if the marker exists, otherwise it fires an event the transcript handles by dropping its window and scrolling once the marker mounts
architecturalRules: interrupt() stays intent-free — no caller may infer "advance" from "stop"
only forceAdvance sets advanceOnComplete (+ advanceOnCompleteStep); a plain Stop leaves it unset and arms no watchdog
whether a settle may consume advanceOnComplete is decided by the advanceOnCompleteStep stamp matching the current step index, not by turnSource
an interrupted settle always parks unless it is also the forced (stamped force-advance) exception, overriding both autoAdvance and a pending plan-approval advance
never advance synchronously under a live turn — flag advanceOnComplete and wait for the turn to settle, with a watchdog as the only fallback
the handleWorkerEnded settle fallback must stay gated on the interrupting set (routine non-error ended events exist)

never call advance() directly on a running step while its turn is active — set advanceOnComplete (+ advanceOnCompleteStep) then call SessionManager.interrupt(); interrupt() no longer implies an advance
the advanceOnCompleteStep stamp, not turnSource, decides whether a settle or the watchdog may consume a pending flag
the watchdog clears turnSource when it fires, so a late arrival from the abandoned turn is ignored by the stamp check
both recoveries are guarded no-ops the user must trigger — the engine never self-heals a stalled step automatically
reuses runStep step-entry behavior (pending) and advance() (done) rather than duplicating hand-off or consolidation logic
a done-at-current-index recovery keys off advancing, never isSessionActive — advance() sets no session status, so the leftover status says nothing about whether an advance is live
advance() must persist the stepIndex bump itself; leaving it to a later broadcast makes the unrecoverable done-at-current-index shape the durable state for the whole consolidation window
the in-flight flag is server-owned broadcast state, never local optimistic UI state
clearing the flag rides the next status broadcast rather than issuing its own — no await may be inserted between the clear and that broadcast
cleared on process restart (constructor load loop) and on hand-off (adoptSynced), never in reconcileWithWorker, which runs far more often and would falsely clear a live advance
runStep's silent early returns now persistMeta before returning, so the cleared flag and bumped stepIndex always reach the client
advance() persists the stepIndex bump immediately rather than letting it ride runStep later broadcast
reuses the transcript-walking pattern from lastAssistantText/summarizeTurn and the one-shot non-agentic query shape from summarizeTurn/autoName
advance() is async; callers fire it with void this.advance(sessionId)
all prompt tokens are filled in one pass over the template (substituteTokens) rather than by chained replaceAll calls; a new token is added to that pass, never appended as another pass
isWorkflowFinished is kept separate from sessionRowMeta's { color, label, actionable } return since projectStatusMeta and alerts.ts consume that shape and workflow-done is not actionable
isWorkflowFinished mirrors workflows.ts advance(): the last step is set done with no further stepIndex bump, so all-done is the only reliable signal

features.name: Turn recovery
features.purpose: Everything that gets a turn back on its feet: detecting and resuming turns that died with the app, a working Retry for every recoverable failure, in-turn recovery from a rejected OAuth token, and the rule that a turn never runs on the unrefreshable ambient ~/.claude login.
businessRules: auto-continue only resumes sessions flagged by the reconcile that is running; a stale flag keeps its banner
autoContinueInterrupted is on unless explicitly false; absent (or no settings.json) means enabled
a resume that throws is contained per session: logged, session put back into the flagged state, later sessions still resume
settings pulled from the storage server are merged field-wise so an older client cannot erase a newer setting by omitting it
interruptedAt clears on prompt, result, markTurnLive and archive/complete, but never on ackSession

the blind-clear timer fires only when no worker ever answered and it never saw an incompatible version; a mismatch is instead surfaced immediately via WorkerStatus.mismatch, not by this timer or the lost deadline
the sidebar row shows the same yellow interrupted dot/badge as the banner via sessionRowMeta, reusing the banner's exact guard, and persists through ackSession the same way
the socket may be down for WORKER_LOST_MS (20s) before it's treated as a real outage, well past an ordinary tsx-watch reconnect (~1-2s)
the worker-lost path flags sessions but never auto-continues them, even with autoContinueInterrupted on; the next real hello resumes them

reconcileWithWorker skips a session that has neither live state nor a local on-disk transcript (SessionManager.ranHere) — it only exists here because storage sync (adoptSynced) adopted it from another machine, and demoting/restamping/auto-continuing it would broadcast and cloud-push a turn this machine never ran; a session with an actual worker report for this pass is still fully reconciled even with no local transcript, since a live report is itself evidence
a cold-start protocol mismatch never sets everConnected, so the outage clock never starts; it's surfaced by WorkerStatus.mismatch instead
exactly one of ConnectionBanner/WorkerBanner/StorageBanner renders at a time; bridge-down outranks worker-down outranks storage-down; scoped to the primary machine only (see multi-machine-client)
every recoverable failure ends on a failure row with a working Retry, in a plain session and inside a running workflow alike
a failed turn never autoAdvances; it parks the step as failed instead, unless an explicit stamped force-advance is already pending
Retry re-runs the right thing: a step that never got a prompt is re-rendered from WorkflowState ('pre-run'); a step whose turn failed is re-sent as a follow-up on the same conversation ('turn')
no auto-retry or backoff — a transient failure (e.g. a 529) is an ordinary failed turn with a manual button
stepFailure is persisted, so a reload while parked in the failed state still shows Retry

an auth-classified turn failure attempts exactly one token refresh, then always rewrites the banner to name the next action (Retry, Sign in, or check your connection) instead of leaving raw CLI text with only Retry
errorKind: 'auth' is set only for the signed-out outcome; refreshed/refresh-failed clear it
the login modal opens off the existing authStatus broadcast, not a new message type, and unlike the hello auto-open it is not deduped
retry stays entirely manual; nothing auto-resumes a failed turn, even after a silent refresh or a fresh sign-in — a login landing later or from another device must not fire N queued turns
errorKind is never set when no AuthManager is wired (ambient-token mode)
every query crash (auth-related or not) still writes a synthetic result event with the raw CLI text preserved verbatim, even after the banner is revised
a clean ended (no error) writes no synthetic result
a signed-in user's turn never runs on ambient ~/.claude credentials; with no app token the turn is refused, since a visible failure with Retry beats a silent 401 loop
a refusal caused by being logged out re-broadcasts the logged-out authStatus so a dismissed login modal reopens; a refusal from a transient refresh failure does not
the bridge-side helper queries (autoName, summarizeTurn, consolidateStepOutput) are best-effort: no token means skip the query, never fall back and never fail the surrounding turn
compactContext still returns a synchronous { ok: true }; an auth refusal after that point surfaces through failTurn, not the { ok: false, code, reason } union
a transiently failed proactive refresh retries on a 60s-doubling ladder capped at 15 minutes; a dead refresh token logs out instead, stopping the chain
accessToken: null in buildQueryOptions is reachable only when no AuthManager is wired at all (tests / embedding), never for a real signed-in user

logins are tracked per OAuth state, so two started at once each keep their own PKCE verifier; completing one clears the rest, unfinished ones expire after 30 minutes, and a paste with no #state falls back to the newest
a content-filter, context-overflow, invalid-request or overloaded failure never implies an automatic retry, backoff, or step advance
auth wins outright when a failure text matches both an auth pattern and a turnFailureKind pattern
the retry hint rides only the re-sent prompt text, never the stored transcript event for the original failed turn
Skip step and the stepper's Approve button send the identical workflowApprove message under the identical gate
a query the bridge cannot vouch for (e.g. no queryTokens entry after a bridge restart) is recycled, not reused
any failed turn drops that session's query, recognised or not, so a single Retry cannot reuse the child that just failed
architecturalRules: adding a field to LiveSessionInfo is not a protocol bump; busy is optional so an old worker stays demote-only instead of losing its socket mid-turn
reconcileWithWorker is the only place that stamps interruptedAt
a result for a flagged session means the flag was wrong (buffered result lands after reconcile) — clear it there rather than adding handshake ordering
onStatusChange (UI health) is kept separate from onWorkerLost (session reconcile) rather than merged
isSelfWorkerSource's check runs before the guard's blanket tool allowlist short-circuit, not after
isSelfWorkerSource is self-locating (import.meta.dirname) rather than threading session/bridge identity into assessToolCall
failTurn is the single funnel for every failure the SDK never reports as a result; public so WorkflowEngine can call it for pre-run failures
the retry router idiom mirrors case 'prompt': WorkflowEngine.retryIfFailed gets first refusal, only false falls through to SessionManager.retryTurn; no new ClientMessage type
lastPromptForRetry is the single source both retryTurn and retryIfFailed read from
the failed park skips setStatus (which clears errorMessage on every transition) and calls persistMeta instead, so the error banner and Retry stay live while the step shows waiting-approval
the client's backward scan for retryKey may only skip 'workflow' and 'context-compact' items; every other kind ends the scan
classification happens at exactly two points: failTurn (covers every funnel caller) and the result branch of handleWorkerEvent, which bypasses failTurn by design
the revision guard (status === 'error' && errorMessage === error) is the entire don't-clobber mechanism, relying on the workflow failed-park path using persistMeta not setStatus
authRecoveryMessage's strings avoid every word AUTH_FAILURE_PATTERNS matches, so a re-failure cannot re-classify itself into a loop
a successful refresh() still does not call emitChange(); the revised banner is the visible signal, not an auth-status broadcast
handleTokenRejected goes through the single-flight refresh() rather than logout() directly, so N simultaneous failures cause one token request and concurrent callers all resolve 'refreshed'
the synthetic result is emitted via emitEvent directly, never routed through handleWorkerEvent, so it cannot re-run turn-settle bookkeeping
SDK/CLI error wording is not a published contract; isAuthFailureMessage can silently stop matching after an upstream change
known limitation: in Compact view the failed row sits inside a collapsed AgentTurn, so SessionView's alert is the always-visible affordance (pre-existing, out of scope)

the never-fall-back guarantee lives in pushTurn, which refuses before reaching buildQueryOptions; there is deliberately no second options builder, which would duplicate the whole option set for one differing key
both turn-start call sites go through pushTurnSafely rather than void this.pushTurn(...), so one place guarantees no unhandled rejection
ownerToken() awaits ensureFreshToken() rather than reading getAccessTokenSync(), so helper queries get the same refresh-on-margin treatment as a real turn
the no-AuthManager branch of pushTurn returns before the first await, keeping that path synchronous for tests that assert an immediate push
the proactive backoff computes its first rung explicitly (null ? RETRY : min(x*2, CAP)) rather than doubling a default, which would skip the 60s rung
getAccessTokenSync() remains on AuthManager but has no production caller; it is kept for the sync-status shape tests rely on

the no-local-history skip is narrow and scoped to reconcileWithWorker only — it does not change adoptSynced or what counts as this instance owning a session; it exists because a flapping worker or duplicate bridge (see hosted-machine-access) turned every reconcile pass into a broadcast/cloud-push storm across sessions this machine never actually ran, feeding the very kind of loop this feature exists to break rather than amplify

queryTokens is bridge-memory only and never persisted, while the worker's live queries outlive a bridge restart — the same asymmetry already documented for interrupted-turn recovery, and why the recycle guard must fail closed on an unknown entry

ensureFreshToken joins an in-flight recovery refresh (refreshInFlight) rather than only checking expiresAt, since expiresAt alone cannot distinguish a merely-unexpired token from one just revoked server-side

features.name: Session and project UI
features.purpose: The shell around a session: persisted unsent drafts, focus on a new session, which session a project switch opens, the project tab's actionable-status dot, and the tool-aware waiting-permission badge.
businessRules: persisted text draft is the full MentionValue (text + ranges), not plain text, so restored pills/expansions stay intact
staged attachments persist too, in IndexedDB rather than localStorage (base64 file data can run tens of MB)
an empty text draft or attachment list is deleted from storage rather than stored empty

Composer's focus effect fires only when session.createdAt is under 5s old; this is its own independent heuristic and no longer shares a threshold with the store's session-select-on-create logic (see session-create-auto-select below) — focus and selection now solve different problems on purpose
switching to an older existing session does not steal focus
auto-selection always excludes archived sessions; completed needs no separate check since the server always archives alongside it
a project whose sessions are all archived auto-selects nothing (empty state) rather than opening an archived one
an explicit selection already in the target project, including an archived session, is never overridden by a tab switch
sort key for most recent is createdAt, matching the sidebar list order
priority highest first: plan ready (violet) > needs answer (teal) > needs approval (sandstone) > needs permission (yellow) > interrupted (yellow) > error (red)
running/done/idle sessions never show a dot
archived sessions are excluded; completed sessions are always archived too, so no separate guard is needed
the active project's tab always shows the plain folder icon, suppressed at render time
opening a project marks its actionable sessions seen; a tab stays quiet until a session reaches a status not yet seen, and a resolved-then-relapsed session counts as new again
seenSessionStatus is in-memory only, so already-seen dots can reappear once after a page reload
ExitPlanMode -> label 'plan ready', violet badge
AskUserQuestion -> label 'needs answer', teal badge
any other tool -> label 'needs permission', yellow badge (unchanged default)
notification body mirrors the sidebar label (capitalized) for waiting-permission sessions

a sessionUpsert only takes the selection when pendingCreate is true AND the session id is not already in seenSessionIds — replaces a comparison of session.createdAt (stamped on the bridge machine) against Date.now() (the browser's clock): hosted, those are different machines, and even a slightly-ahead bridge clock made every upsert look 'just created' forever, so any session re-entering the map stole the selection

pendingCreate is set by markSessionCreatePending() (called by every createSession sender: the sidebar's New session button/menu, and the recipe-run path already selects explicitly via its own sessionId and does not need it) and expires on its own after 15s if no matching upsert ever arrives

seenSessionIds is maintained by both the hello reducer and sessionUpsert, so a session that leaves and re-enters the map — deleted then resurrected, or replayed by a duplicate hello — is never treated as new again

a repeated hello (same session/project signature as the last one applied) is inert: sessions, transcriptLoaded and contextBreakdowns are left untouched, while every other field (usage, worker/storage health, auth) still applies as normal — the relay replays open (and its full hello) for every live channel on any bridge attach or takeover, and wholesale-replacing state on each one is what turned two alternating bridge snapshots into a self-sustaining flicker loop across sessions and transcript reloads

send() (ws.ts) returns false when the socket is not open and the message is not a prompt (prompts alone queue for replay); the caller sets actionError so a dropped control message — e.g. a delete sent while disconnected — is visible instead of a console.warn nobody saw

deleting a session shows a loading state on its own row and leaves the row in place until the sessionDeleted echo removes it — no optimistic removal, so a delete that silently failed to send is never mistaken for one that worked

archived sessions in the sidebar render 20 at a time behind a 'Show N more' button instead of the full archived list, since lines.showArchived defaults to on and a long-lived project can accumulate hundreds of them
architecturalRules: text drafts use a single lines.drafts JSON map keyed by session id, following the existing store.ts convention (e.g. lines.openFiles) rather than one key per session
attachment drafts use IndexedDB (db lines-drafts, store attachments, keyed by session id) instead of localStorage, since size is the reason attachments are staged as raw base64 in the first place
reuses the store's existing justCreated 5s threshold instead of adding a new is-new flag or protocol field
membership check reuses sessionsInProject rather than an inline cwd comparison, so it stays key-aware like every other project-scoped scan
format.ts never imports store.ts; projectStatusMeta takes plain SessionMeta[] plus a seen map to keep that dependency edge one-way
the priority table is built from the same waitingPermissionMeta/STATUS_META entries sessionRowMeta uses, so a tab dot can never drift from the sidebar dot it points at
seenSessionStatus is maintained in a single store subscription rather than at each mutation site that could change what counts as seen
pendingPermissionTool rides the existing sessionUpsert broadcast, no new message type
cleared centrally in setStatus for any non-waiting-permission status, plus the worker-reconcile and sync-adopt paths that can force waiting-permission back to idle out from under a live turn
concurrent permission asks on the same session: last askPermission call wins the label/color, consistent with pre-existing status-overwrite behavior

sessionRowMeta is the single row-presentation entry point: waitingPermissionMeta first, then the interrupted-turn-recovery yellow state, then the plain per-status table (moved into format.ts from Sidebar.tsx)

helloSignature is a cheap string (each session's id:updatedAt joined, plus project paths) rather than a hash of the whole hello payload, precisely so volatile fields (usage, worker/storage health) stay outside it and keep applying on every hello regardless of the short-circuit

store changes here (the hello short-circuit, pendingCreate/seenSessionIds) are pure reducer logic with no web test harness backing them (web/ has no test runner) — the highest-risk, least-covered part of this feature; verified manually

SessionRow is memoized — selecting a different session or any sessions-map update (e.g. a live turn ticking status) otherwise re-rendered every row in the list regardless of the size of the session being switched to; the memo relies on `session` keeping its object identity when unchanged, which sessionUpsert already guarantees by only replacing the entry that changed

features.name: Transcript rendering
features.purpose: How the transcript is drawn: one shared markdown renderer with a bubble only for user prompts, structured per-tool field lists instead of raw JSON, and subagent runs nested under their spawning card.
businessRules: user and agent text render markdown instead of plain preformatted text; single newlines collapse and raw HTML tags are dropped
code blocks wrap long lines (white-space: pre-wrap, overflow-wrap: anywhere) instead of scrolling horizontally
only the user prompt renders as a bubble (right-aligned, capped at 80% column width); agent output is unwrapped and flush-left with nesting shown by order/expand affordance, not indentation
every tool's expanded body shows a structured field list, never raw JSON by default; raw JSON is one toggle away for every tool with no exceptions

a tool call already fully explained elsewhere in the row loses its expand affordance instead of showing an empty/redundant body: a successful edit (diff button covers it) loses only the chevron; a settled (answered, non-error) AskUserQuestion loses the row too and renders as just the always-open review

every AskUserQuestion call is isolated into its own single-tool group and treated as a foldAgentTurns boundary (like a pending ExitPlanMode), so it always renders as its own top-level transcript item regardless of tool-grouping level or Compact folding
an AskUserQuestion call's answer is read from its tool result's prose, not its input — the input only ever contains the questions asked

a subagent's assistant text and tool calls are never counted as main-agent output: workflow step output, the turn summary, and the live context-usage reading are all derived from main-agent messages only
a subagent's tool calls and text nest under its spawning card, never inline in the main transcript or folded into the main agent's tool group
a subagent cannot itself spawn another subagent (harness restriction), so nesting is one level deep in practice, though the data model is recursive
a message whose parent_tool_use_id names a spawn block not present in the transcript falls back to the main sink instead of being dropped
a spawn card leads with description, not the tool name; an unmapped or plugin-scoped subagent_type degrades to a generic agent badge (never hidden, never a crash)
the main agent and a subagent share the same badge icon but never the same color, so who is running reads from color alone before any label
in the interactive OptionCard, the checkbox/radio is a non-interactive indicator; the wrapping button is the sole click target, so onChange must not be added back to the control itself

code-block syntax highlighting (rehype-highlight) is deferred: first paint renders without it, then an idle callback (2s timeout fallback) upgrades the document in place — the highlighter only adds classes inside an already-laid-out <pre>, so it cannot reflow the transcript; a document with no code block skips the deferral and renders with the full plugin set immediately
architecturalRules: user and agent transcript text share one markdown renderer instead of separate text-rendering paths; ColorizedText.tsx deleted as dead code
user bubble Paper needs minWidth: 0 alongside maxWidth: '80%' so wide content (e.g. a code block or one long unbroken token) can't win over max-width via min-content sizing
compact markdown rhythm overrides Mantine spacing variables scoped to .md-body rather than CSS selectors, because Typography's list rule outranks a .md-body ul selector override on specificity
collapsible transcript rows (agent turns, tool groups, tool calls) share one borderless .tx-row convention: no Paper/border, CSS-only hover, and no accumulating indentation

a collapsed row's body unmounts instead of only being CSS-hidden, so per-row state that must survive collapse/expand lives in a module-scope sticky map, not component state; sub-toggles inside an already-expanded body (a spawn card's prompt disclosure, every tool card's raw-input toggle) are deliberately plain useState, not sticky, since resetting on close is expected there.

react-window (or similar list virtualization) is still rejected — it would break updateProgress's workflow-step-marker scan, the scrollHeight-based auto-pin/ResizeObserver, and find-in-page; a simple tail window (last ~40 top-level items, growing on idle backfill or scroll-to-top) supersedes lazy-mounted bodies alone once a real session's markdown mount cost dominates — see transcript-performance.md

toolFields degrades instead of failing: an unclassifiable value becomes a capped json field rather than throwing or being skipped, since tool input shapes (especially MCP tools) are not controlled by this code
OptionCard gained a readOnly prop instead of being duplicated into a second component, so a settled answer looks exactly like the choice that produced it
the raw-input toggle shows even for an empty ({}) input, unlike PermissionPrompt's equivalent guard — consistency across every tool card was chosen over hiding a no-op toggle
existing transcripts already carry parent_tool_use_id on disk (persisted verbatim by the worker), so this feature is a pure read-side reinterpretation with no new capture and no migration
no agents option was added to buildQueryOptions; subagent definitions are inherited via settingSources, the same mechanism that already inherits the rest of the preset

the spawn tool's name is not a stable literal: the harness emits 'Agent', the SDK's own AgentInput type and docs call it 'Task', and both appear in persisted transcripts, so every consumer matches via isAgentTool() rather than one string
agentMeta/MAIN_AGENT_META is the single source of truth for agent icon/color, read by both the settled card and the live ActivityRow so they cannot drift apart

parseTaskInput never throws and never assumes a field is present, since AgentInput gains fields the map won't know about (effort is the live example) — this is why the raw-input toggle stays reachable behind every spawn card
nested rendering is threaded down as a renderNested callback rather than a new shared module, since ToolCallCard cannot import Transcript.tsx's Item without an import cycle

reconcileItems (transcript.ts) hands a rebuilt item back its previous object identity when every field buildTranscript can later mutate in place is unchanged (ToolBlock.result/isError/snapshot/children, permission .resolution/.data, ResultItem.summary, streaming/assistant text) — this is what lets memo on Item/AgentTurn/ToolGroup/ToolCallCard skip work and what lets the toolDiffCache WeakMap survive a rebuild instead of recomputing every whole-file diff per event; missing a mutated field here means a changed row silently keeps rendering its old content

the renderNested callback threaded from Transcript into ToolGroup/ToolCallCard must stay referentially stable across renders (a useCallback keyed on sessionId, reached through a ref so it can call itself for a nested subagent transcript) — a fresh closure every render defeats those components' memo silently, with nothing erroring

the workflow progress bar (updateProgress) reads which steps have started from the item list itself (a 'workflow' item with event 'started'), not from rendered [data-workflow-step] DOM marker positions, since the tail window can clip an early marker out of the DOM entirely; a clipped-but-started step's segment reports as fully filled rather than 0% filled; clicking a stepper step whose marker isn't mounted goes through revealWorkflowStep()/REVEAL_STEP_EVENT (web/src/lib/workflowReveal.ts) instead of a direct querySelector

features.name: Agent memory sync
features.purpose: Sync ~/.claude agent memory (user CLAUDE.md and per-project auto-memory) across a user's machines via the storage server, keeping disk as the SDK-facing cache and Postgres as the cross-machine source of truth.
businessRules: only ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md and ~/.claude/projects/<slug>/memory/** are synced; cwd-local CLAUDE.md/.claude, settings.json, and credentials are never touched
per-file entry cap 256 KB; full-snapshot push additionally caps total payload at ~1.5 MB, dropping largest files first
server prunes tombstones older than ~30 days
conflict resolution is per-file last-write-wins by file mtime; the losing side's edit is silently dropped
architecturalRules: reuses the existing StorageSyncClient debounce-and-push pattern and syncNow pull-then-push cycle instead of a new sync mechanism
push is triggered from the SessionManager result-sniffing callback in userContext.ts, not sessions.ts or worker.ts, keeping the worker thin
project-scoped files are keyed by the machine-independent ProjectKeyRegistry key, falling back to a raw slug key when unresolved
the ~/.claude/projects/<slug>/memory/ layout and path-to-slug derivation are Claude CLI/SDK-internal, not a published contract

features.name: Cloud sync: session push budgeting and delete tombstones
features.purpose: Push a user's SessionMeta list to the storage server without re-sending rows it already has and without exceeding the storage server's request body limit, and make a session delete stick across every machine syncing that account rather than being silently re-pushed by whichever one hasn't heard about it yet.
businessRules: a bulk push filters out sessions whose updatedAt/createdAt is not newer than the last accepted push, since storage rows are LWW upserts and re-sending unchanged rows is pure waste
a meta with neither updatedAt nor createdAt is always pushed
a single session whose own JSON exceeds the push budget is dropped from the cloud push (with a one-time warning), never blocking its siblings; its local copy is untouched
a rejected chunk's sessions are retried on the next flush, not dropped
a storage 413 (entity.too.large) answers JSON {error: 'payload too large'} instead of a generic 500 HTML page

a session delete is a soft delete (Session.deletedAt) in storage, never a hard delete — a hard delete leaves peers nothing to adopt, so whichever machine still holds the row pushes it right back on its next sync

DELETE is idempotent: a repeat keeps the original deletedAt stamp rather than advancing it, since the bridge retries a delete until storage confirms it and moving the tombstone forward each retry would re-notify every peer
GET /sessions serves tombstoned rows inside the ordinary delta window (carrying deletedAt in ms) — that is the only way a peer learns about a delete at all
PUT (bulk or single) refuses to resurrect a row whose deletedAt is at or after the pushed updatedAt; a write genuinely newer than the delete does bring the row back and clears the tombstone
the bridge keeps its own tombstone map (id -> deletedAt ms), persisted alongside sessions.json and pruned past ~30 days on load

adoptSynced returns early when a pulled session's stamp does not beat an existing local tombstone — the branch the ordinary LWW check never reached before, since that check only ran when a local copy of the session already existed
applyRemoteDelete records a tombstone even for a session this machine never held, so a slower third machine's later push can't resurrect it here either
a delete issued while pulled state is being applied, or before there is a token to send it with, is queued (pendingDeletes) rather than dropped, and rides the next flush/sync instead of being lost
a bulk push (reconnect) filters out any session whose delete is still unconfirmed, so the whole-list push can't undo a delete that raced it
architecturalRules: SESSIONS_PUSH_MAX_BYTES (1.5MB) mirrors the same headroom-under-2mb constant style as TOTAL_MAX_BYTES in server/src/memory.ts
chunk sends are sequential inside the debounce timer callback, not parallel, so one failure doesn't strand the rest silently
pushSessions owns the dedup filter; userContext.ts's syncNow still hands it the full session list — sync.ts keeps sole ownership of what actually goes on the wire
the real growth driver (WorkflowState.outputs/lastStepOutput, uncapped in server/src/workflows.ts) is not capped by this change — deferred as a follow-up

the row-level rules (LWW upsert, soft delete, resurrect guard, wire shape) live in storage/src/sessionRows.ts rather than inline in the /sessions routes, so they're unit-testable without a Clerk token — /sessions itself stays Clerk-gated and just calls through
flushSessions re-checks pendingDeletes per chunk, after the batch was drained but before each chunk's own await, so a delete issued while an earlier chunk is in flight is not undone by a later one
SessionManager's sessions map and tombstone map are always written together (a single writeState), so they can never desync on disk
deleteSession and applyRemoteDelete share a private forget() that only tears down live state that actually exists, so a remote tombstone for a session this machine never ran costs nothing

features.name: Storage availability banner
features.purpose: Classify why the bridge's storage-server link is down, wait out a routine expired-token 401 instead of raising the "cloud sync unavailable" banner, actively re-probe once down so recovery is noticed within seconds, and persist a bounded failure log a user can read and copy from Settings without a bridge console.
businessRules: a single auth (401/403) failure does not raise the banner; only AUTH_GRACE_MS (90s) of continuous auth failures does, and any 2xx/304 resets that clock
while down, a GET /settings probe fires every PROBE_INTERVAL_MS (15s) so recovery is reflected within seconds instead of waiting for the next incidental pull/push
the probe targets /settings, not /health, since /health sits above storage's Clerk gate and would falsely clear an auth-caused outage
sync-log.jsonl only grows on a failed request or an availability transition, capped at ~256 KB and trimmed to its newer half on overflow
a soft-error request still marks the link available and never touches the auth-grace clock, since a soft 401 is not evidence the token is good
architecturalRules: classifyStatus/classifyError are pure exported functions, unit-testable without constructing a client
appendLog is injected with the same shape and default (() => {}) as the existing persistMarks parameter, so sync.ts still imports no fs
the probe timer is unref()'d like every other StorageSyncClient timer, started only on the down transition and stopped only on the up transition
no storage-server change: no Prisma migration, no storage/ deploy coupling

features.name: App data root
features.purpose: Machine-global directory (~/.lines-app) holding all server-side app state.
businessRules: app data root is ~/.lines-app
'local' user uses the flat root; real user ids live under ~/.lines-app/users/{id}
machine-wide assets (vendored plugins) live directly under the root, shared across users
architecturalRules: all persistent paths derive from APP_ROOT / userStoreRoot; never hardcode the home-directory path elsewhere

createStore keeps an in-memory, per-user transcript cache (raw lines + lazily-parsed events) revalidated by statSync mtime/size and bounded by count and byte size; it assumes this process is the sole writer of transcripts/*.jsonl
sessions.json writes are compact (not pretty-printed) and debounced via SessionManager.persist/flushPersist, coalescing a burst of status transitions into one write without delaying the broadcast

the sole-writer assumption is enforced, not just assumed: ~/.lines-app/bridge.lock is claimed by every bridge unconditionally (relaying or not), so a second bridge process refuses to start rather than becoming that second writer — see hosted-machine-access.md

features.name: @mention support in prompts
features.purpose: Reference a documented feature or project file inline in the composer prompt via @mention, expanded to context text at send time.
businessRules: mentions are expanded into plain prompt text client-side before send; server and worker never resolve mentions[], only the sidecar for display
a stale feature/file reference degrades to a harmless stale text block rather than blocking send
/find respects .gitignore via git ls-files, falls back to a bounded walk outside a repo, capped at 20000 files
architecturalRules: new mention kinds are added as one more MentionProvider entry, no switch-over-kind elsewhere
pill ranges are a derived view synced to the authoritative plain-text string by prefix/suffix diffing, not a second source of truth
no contenteditable/rich-text dependency; pills are a cosmetic mirror-div overlay behind a plain textarea

/find, /file, /tree share one corsFor() helper and one resolveWorkspacePath() root restriction (now in server/src/workspacePaths.ts), which also allows a plan-directory path outside every root (isPlanPath)

features.name: Workflow task attachments
features.purpose: Carry image attachments sent with a workflow's task description into step 0's prompt instead of silently dropping them.
businessRules: attachments ride the entry step (step 0) only; later steps do not re-carry the original file
a non-fresh later step inherits the image for free via the live conversation; a freshStart step gets only the compact previous/diff hand-off, never the original attachment
mentions[] stay out of scope: display-only and already expanded into prompt text client-side
a step 0 that parks (waiting-approval) drops the attachment with no transcript trace; the user must re-attach
architecturalRules: attachment handling stays entirely in SessionManager.prompt; worker.ts does no attachment handling

features.name: Local dev orchestration (Tilt)
features.purpose: Run the four local dev processes (worker, bridge, storage, web) via Tilt with readiness probes, a loud preflight, automatic Prisma generation, and a live-togglable freeze on worker/bridge hot reload.
businessRules: tilt up gates only storage on .env completeness (DATABASE_URL/DIRECT_URL/CLERK_SECRET_KEY); bridge/worker/web stay reachable even when storage config is missing
freezing worker or bridge reload swaps which npm script the resource runs, it does not change Tilt's own watch behavior
toggling freeze restarts that resource once, at the moment it's toggled, dropping any in-flight agent turn on the worker
freezing worker while bridge stays hot and editing workerProtocol.ts produces a visible protocol-version mismatch in the bridge log until the worker is restarted by hand
web is excluded from the freeze options since Vite HMR never restarts the dev server
a pull that changes only package-lock.json triggers nothing; run tilt trigger install by hand

pair-device (npm run pair -w server) is always declared but never auto_init - triggered by hand when a code expires or a machine is revoked, not part of bringing the stack up; idempotent, prints 'already paired' and exits 0 on a claimed device
desktop-package (npm run package -w desktop) is the same shape as pair-device - manual, never part of tilt up - and exists so the DMG build is discoverable from Tilt at all

RELAY_URL set without STORAGE_URL warns rather than failing preflight - the bridge would dial a hosted relay while syncing to the local storage default, splitting one machine's data across two databases

when RELAY_URL in .env points at a non-loopback host and ~/.lines-app/bridge.lock names a live process, preflight warns (naming the tray app if instance:'desktop', or naming any other holder as one that will refuse with exit 78) rather than failing; a stale/absent/unparseable lock is silent

LINES_INSTANCE is not set anywhere in this Tiltfile despite older comments claiming Tilt sets it to 'dev' — web/vite.config.ts resolves /__bridge from the same variable, so pinning it for the bridge alone would break dev-server discovery
architecturalRules: no deps= on the four service resources — tsx watch/Vite own file-watching, not Tilt
PORT is injected per resource via serve_env, never a shared env block
preflight reads .env key names only, never values, into any Tilt spec/log/UI button

the Freeze/Resume UI buttons and the --no-reload CLI flag are two entry points into one FROZEN state, reconciled by re-invoking tilt args with the full current flag set rather than mutating Tilt state directly
no resource watches a file its own cmd writes — install's deps list the five workspace manifests but omit package-lock.json, which npm install itself rewrites and would retrigger the resource forever
resource_deps gates only the first build after tilt up; a later re-run of install does not cascade to prisma-generate or the four service resources

whether the bridge talks to a hosted install is not a Tilt flag - it follows RELAY_URL in .env, read by the bridge's own dotenv; STORAGE_URL is injected into serve_env only as a default, so an explicit .env value is never overridden

features.name: Context window
features.purpose: Live context-window occupancy in the composer with a per-category breakdown, plus manual compaction, a near-limit warning, and readable transcript events for both manual and CLI auto-compaction.
businessRules: occupancy is sourced from the SDK's /context control request (getContextUsage()) when a live query exists, never from result.usage, which is cumulative across every API call in the turn rather than a point-in-time reading
the ContextUsage fallback (derived from the last assistant message's usage) is used only when no live query is available
no reading yet means no chip, in both fallback and SDK modes
unknown model context window shows raw token counts with no ring rather than guessing a denominator
category/component rows must sum to the shown total; any SDK-reported vs component-sum mismatch is surfaced as an explicit residual row instead of hidden
deferred categories are excluded from the total and from free space, and shown with no percentage share, to avoid double-counting
the persisted SessionMeta.contextSummary is capped and holds no per-item detail since it is synced and written to disk; per-item detail is fetched on demand and never persisted
a hover-triggered summary refresh only broadcasts/syncs when the summary actually changed
resetting a session's Claude conversation (workflow fresh-start step) stamps contextResetAt; readings older than that render as stale until the next turn reports

Lines does not set autoCompactEnabled and has no control over the CLI's own background auto-compaction; the hover card's auto-compact row is a straight passthrough of the CLI's own settingSources-resolved setting, shown even when off

Lines never fires compaction itself — only a manual button and a passive warning badge, since it is irreversible, lossy, and billable; this is distinct from the CLI's own background auto-compaction, which Lines does not control

the manual button's disabled state always carries a specific reason (turn running, workflow step parked, no session yet, no reading yet, or the SDK explicitly reported the compaction failed) via one shared contextCompactBlock predicate
the unsupported latch requires an explicit SDK compact_result:'failed' — a turn settling with neither a boundary nor a status verdict is inconclusive and leaves the button enabled

the unsupported latch is scoped to the CLI conversation that produced it: cleared on resetClaudeSession, on bridge restart, and when adopting a synced session, so it never survives past the process/conversation that saw the failure
a workflow step parked waiting-approval blocks the manual button but not the CLI's own background auto-compaction
a compaction is invisible to every workflow turn scan (consolidateStepOutput, lastAssistantText, summarizeTurn, retryTurn) via withoutCompactSpans, but never stripped from permission bookkeeping
architecturalRules: the bridge-worker protocol gained a generic ask/askResult request-response method rather than a one-off message type, so future control requests do not require another PROTOCOL_VERSION bump (which restarts the worker and drops in-flight turns)
the worker returns raw SDK JSON from ask; all normalization lives in server/src/contextBreakdown.ts as pure, defensively-coerced functions, keeping the worker's import graph unchanged
the existing cumulative fields (lastTokens, totalTokens) are untouched; this feature adds a parallel occupancy reading rather than altering the billing one
compactContext is a dedicated SessionManager method, not a call to prompt() — a compaction carries no 'user' transcript event and must not auto-name the session or touch the queue
one shared predicate (contextCompactBlock) backs the server-side guard, the button's disabled state, and its tooltip

naming: transcript event kind 'context-compact', payload ContextCompactData, SessionMeta.contextCompact — all contextCompact-prefixed, distinct from the unrelated compactionLevel (transcript display density)

the browser's buildTranscript mirrors withoutCompactSpans: events inside an open compact span are dropped from the rendered transcript, not just hidden by the marker pair — except a failed result, which closes the span like a 'user' event does

features.name: Conversational workflow/step editing (in-process MCP tools)
features.purpose: Expose workflow/step list/read/create/update/delete as in-process MCP tools (mcp__lines__*) so a session can discuss and edit its own workflows in conversation instead of only via the WorkflowEditor modal; writes are permission-gated, reads are not.
businessRules: mutations address a workflow by id, or by a name unique among owned workflows; a name match against another user's published workflow is refused as read-only, never silently forked
create_workflow/update_workflow/save_step are rejected before WorkflowEngine.save() on a shared workflowValidation.ts failure, with one actionable error string
update_workflow's steps argument replaces the whole list, no patch-by-index
resolveWorkflowRef must catch the id-belongs-to-a-shared-workflow case before saveWorkflow runs, since WorkflowEngine.save() silently no-ops for it
list/read tools cap results at 100 rows (default 50)
a bridge gone mid-call answers after MCP_TOOL_FALLBACK_MS (30s) with an error result rather than parking the turn indefinitely
architecturalRules: tool names/descriptions/schemas live entirely on the bridge (mcpWorkflowTools.ts) and are hot-reloadable; only the workflow-agnostic conversion (workerMcp.ts) and protocol shape (workerProtocol.ts) sit in the worker's minimal import graph
PROTOCOL_VERSION bumped 2->3 for the optional push.tools field, so a bridge/worker skew is a loud mismatch instead of silently tool-less sessions
RPC_FALLBACK table excludes canUseTool on purpose - the SDK parks it with no deadline since a permission request must wait for a human
workflowCommands.ts imports UserContext type-only to avoid a runtime cycle with userContext.ts

shared/workflowValidation.ts is re-exported from shared/types.ts as that file's last statement, an intentional import cycle safe only while workflowValidation.ts never reads types.ts bindings at its own top level
the web WorkflowEditor draft (useWorkflowDraft.ts) was not migrated onto shared/workflowValidation.ts in this change; the two validators can drift

features.name: Brand logo assets
features.purpose: Renders the Lines brand mark across the tab-bar header, browser tab favicon, and desktop notification icon; there is no wordmark anywhere, baked or DOM.
businessRules: the header, favicon, and notification icon all use the same mark art now - no separate lockup - logo-mark.png for the header, logo-mark-solid.png/favicon.png for the other two
favicon.png and logo-mark-solid.png are the same art at two paths because index.html needs a /public URL while alerts.ts wants a Vite asset import
the header is height-driven (height 24, width auto) inside a plate with padding 4 and borderRadius 6
alt="Lines" on the header is the only accessible name for the brand
architecturalRules: the white plate in ProjectTabs is load-bearing: logo-mark.png is transparent with no background of its own, so without the plate the art would sit directly on the dark header; the plate also supplies the header's corner rounding since that asset carries no baked mask

logo-mark-solid.png/favicon.png bake their own rounded-rect corner mask (RGBA), unlike the header asset, because nothing downstream - the favicon <link>, the Notification icon - can round them at render time
link.type must track the real bytes: index.html declares image/png and restorePlain resets to image/png after render installs a data URL
committed PNGs are cropped derivatives of a single 1254x1254 RGB-on-white source that is not in the repo; a future re-crop or re-tone must start from that source, not from the committed derivatives

features.name: Multi-root projects
features.purpose: Let one project tab span more than one folder, so every session created in it can read and write in all of them with the same auto-approve behavior as the primary, and the file tree, @mention, and /find see every root.
businessRules: the primary path is the project's sole identity; extra roots widen what its sessions may read/write, but every session's cwd stays the primary
writes in an extra root auto-approve in auto mode exactly like the primary; the sensitive-path override (~/.ssh, ~/.aws, .env) still wins regardless of which root a path resolves under
one root belongs to exactly one project; roots may not nest within a project
an empty roots list escalates every file tool - the guard fails toward prompting, never toward silently trusting nothing
@mention's feature provider stays primary-root-only; only the file provider is multi-root
removing a root only narrows what the project's sessions may reach; nothing on disk is touched, and the learned project key for that path is kept
architecturalRules: roots are resolved at use time from the project record (rootsForCwd), never snapshotted onto SessionMeta, which is synced and must keep its existing shape
additionalDirectories is omitted (not []) for a single-root project, so a single-root session's serialized query options stay byte-identical to before this feature
the guard's three exported functions take roots: string[], not an optional 5th parameter after cwd
projects.json stays local-only (never synced); only the resolved project-key map is synced
deliberately does not reuse resolveProjectKey for root membership - that key's --show-prefix keeps monorepo siblings apart, the opposite of what one workspace tab needs

features.name: Multi-repo commits
features.purpose: Group a multi-root session's folders into git commit units by work tree (not by project), give a workflow step's {diff} a per-repo section, and add a {roots} token so a step can scope every git command with -C <repo root>, since additionalDirectories never moves the Bash shell out of the session's primary cwd.
businessRules: commit units come from git rev-parse --show-toplevel, never from resolveProjectKey, whose --show-prefix component deliberately keeps monorepo siblings apart
two roots that resolve to the same work tree are one commit unit; two separate work trees are two
a root that isn't inside any git work tree is never a commit unit
{roots} is not a hand-off token: a template using only {roots} with freshStart on still gets the normal {previous}/{diff} auto-prepend
a single repo produces no '# repo:' header in {diff} - existing single-root workflows see byte-identical prompts
the MAX_DIFF_CHARS budget for {diff} is shared across every commit unit, not multiplied by the repo count, with unused share redistributed to repos that overflowed theirs
architecturalRules: repo-grouping/diff logic (git.ts) stays pure git, with no prompt formatting; {roots}'s rendering lives in workflows.ts
the shared git() helper now has a timeout, since this feature multiplies git calls on the step-entry path the user waits through at every approval gap
diffBaselines is additive alongside the deprecated diffBaseline inside the synced WorkflowState; writers only ever set diffBaselines, the legacy field is read-only
MAX_UNTRACKED (new-file cap per diff) is per repo, not per workflow

features.name: Git worktrees
features.purpose: Run a session in its own linked git worktree instead of sharing one checkout with every other session in the project; attribution to the parent tab without widening what the session's roots may reach. A per-session worktree starts detached and gets a lines/<title> branch once the session's auto-title resolves, so nothing is ever renamed.
businessRules: attribution, not capability: a worktree session's project tab widens, its roots never do — projectRoots must never return a worktree path
one path, one owner, and no nesting, extending the same rule multi-root-projects applies to roots
a per-session worktree starts detached; its branch is cut once the session's auto-title resolves and is never renamed after; a worktree the user named explicitly gets its branch immediately
every branch Lines mints on its own initiative is namespaced lines/… (LINES_BRANCH_PREFIX); a branch the user typed into the create form is untouched
removal is always explicit; git branch -d only when asked and only for a branch createdByLines; never -D
removal is refused while any non-archived session's cwd is inside the worktree, unless force
deleting or archiving a session never touches its worktree — the record renders 'orphaned', one click from Remove
git is the source of truth; Project.worktrees is a cache reconciled on openProject; a worktree adopted from outside Lines never gets createdByLines
explicit create fails on a taken path/branch; the per-session auto path uniquifies (-2, -3…) instead
a managed worktree (under WORKTREE_ROOT) is never added to the recent-directories list, since opening it as its own project tab would double-count every session in it
architecturalRules: runGit (throws, stderr in the message) is for mutating git only; the existing git() (swallows every failure to '') stays read-only
Lines' own worktree operations go through worktreeCommands, never Bash, so assessToolCall never sees them; the two new BASH_RULES entries govern only an agent running git itself
WorktreeDeps (run, repoRoot, ensureParent) is the one seam every command function takes, mirroring GitRun in worktrees.ts
defaultWorktreePath groups by repo basename under WORKTREE_ROOT, not full repo path, so a name collision is resolved by the existing uniquifier
SessionManager.onAutoNamed is a callback wired in userContext.ts, not a direct call from sessions.ts into worktreeCommands.ts, since that layer needs a whole UserContext

features.name: Documentation reader
features.purpose: In-app reader for a project's docs/** markdown corpus: a doc tree, an index.json-driven feature-card home, full-text search, and cross-links that navigate inside the reader instead of opening the source-file preview.
businessRules: an index entry whose doc is missing from the bundle still renders as a card with a 'no doc' badge; a bundle doc no entry claims lists under 'Other documents'; a missing/unparseable index degrades to a plain document list
a markdown link target always resolves to kind: 'doc' and opens inside the reader even when the target isn't in this corpus, surfacing a 'not in this corpus' panel instead of a source-preview 404
a link that escapes the docs root, or isn't markdown, opens the existing file-preview modal instead
no project open, or no docs/ folder in the active project, shows an empty state instead of an error boundary
architecturalRules: one bundle request (GET /docs?path=) powers the tree, cards, search and cross-links; no per-file fan-out and no separate search route
/docs sits inside the same corsFor() + resolveWorkspacePath gate as /file, /tree and /find
collectDocs never follows symlinked files or directories, closing an exfiltration path a prefix-based containment check would otherwise miss
pure doc logic (link resolution, title/summary extraction, search ranking) lives in shared/types.ts so node:test can cover it
Markdown gained one optional onLinkClick prop instead of being forked; absent, every transcript call site keeps the existing openFilePreview behavior
the three global modals (MonacoPreviewModal, LoginModal, GuardAllowlistReviewModal) are mounted at the App root instead of inside Shell, so they still work on /docs

features.name: Hosted machine access
features.purpose: The whole path from a browser anywhere to the agent on the user's own machine: ephemeral local ports, the browser-bridge contract, the outbound relay, device pairing, and the UI gate that picks which machine you are talking to.
businessRules: fromAgent only accepts a frame from the socket the hub currently calls its agent; a superseded (or half-dead) bridge that keeps writing cannot inject state into a live browser channel or close a channel now owned by the bridge that replaced it
attachAgent terminates (not just closes) the predecessor it supersedes, so a takeover cannot leave the loser's socket lingering OPEN on the relay

the per-agent re-verify tick and health/ping interval both bail out the instant their own socket is no longer the hub's agent, so a superseded socket's still-running timer can never drop the hub — or evict the browser channels — out from under the bridge that replaced it
a duplicate agent attach for a device (attachAgent superseding a live one) logs distinctly from a first attach, naming the running attach count

the relay's public health endpoint (GET /) keeps its exact unauthenticated shape; presenting the correct x-relay-secret (constant-time compared) additionally returns hubs, a per-device summary (deviceId, online, channel count, agentAttaches, lastAttachAt) for triage — agentAttaches climbing on an otherwise-idle paired device is the tell for two bridges fighting over one identity

the bridge rejects a duplicate open for a channel id it already serves (logging a warning) rather than building a second RelayChannel — every agent attach replays open for all live channels, so a takeover (or any re-announcement) re-delivers ids already held, and building a second link means a second full hello down a socket that never reconnected
RelayClient.connect() closes any pre-existing socket (and drops its channels) before dialling a new one, so one RelayClient instance can never hold two live sockets for the same device

every bridge takes this machine's single-instance lock (~/.lines-app/bridge.lock, pid+startedAt+instance+deviceId) unconditionally, relaying or not, claimed atomically ('wx'); on collision a live instance:'desktop' holder is preempted (SIGTERM, cross-checked against its own published runtime file first) since the tray is the only supervisor that can stand down and re-arm, any other live holder gets a bounded ~2s retry window (for a tsx watch successor meeting a still-exiting predecessor) before the new process exits EXIT_BRIDGE_LOCK_HELD (78) naming the holder

LINES_ALLOW_MULTIPLE_BRIDGES=1 is the deliberate escape hatch that skips the single-instance lock entirely (no read, no write), for tests and any intentionally-run second bridge; it must never be set in a real deployment

RelayClient no longer resets its reconnect backoff on 'open' — only a socket that survives RELAY_STABLE_MS does, on close, since a supersede close always follows a successful open and the old reset let two bridges fight at the retry floor forever; SUPERSEDE_LIMIT consecutive supersedes with no stable socket escalates the re-dial cap to SUPERSEDE_CAP_MS, resetting the moment a dial lands a stable link
register is unauthenticated - the machine has no user yet and a code is worthless until claimed; re-registering an already-claimed AND UNREVOKED device is refused (409) rather than silently re-bound
re-registering a REVOKED device clears its stale userId/revokedAt and issues a fresh code - otherwise a revoked machine could never be claimed again, since claim and verify both refuse a revoked row
claim/verify answer the same 'unknown or expired code' for absent, expired, and revoked, so a distinct 'expired' reply can't confirm a guessed code had once been real

revoking a device tombstones it (revokedAt) rather than deleting the row, so it stays an audit trail; it stops the device reconnecting AND ends a live connection within RELAY_REVERIFY_MS, since the relay re-checks each attached device's claim on a timer rather than only on attach

the re-verify tick is asymmetric with attach on purpose: attach fails closed on a refusal OR an outage, but a live device is dropped only on an explicit 403 - treating a storage blip as a refusal would kick every user off their own machine
