the relay pings its attached agent and terminate()s one silent for ~2 missed pings; without it a half-open socket leaves the device looking online forever and the browser spinning with no hello
the bridge terminates its own relay socket after LINES_RELAY_IDLE_MS of silence and re-dials - also the macOS-sleep fix, since the wall-clock tick fires late on wake

POST /v1/devices/unpair is authenticated by the device secret (the machine holds no user token) and must stay internet-reachable, unlike verify; every failure answers the same opaque 403 and it returns no pairing code, leaving register as the one code-issuing path
GET /v1/devices never returns secretHash
if storage is unreachable the relay refuses the device rather than admitting it
the desktop shell re-registers an unclaimed device on a timer and on demand to keep a valid code on screen with no app restart, relying on register's re-issue (not 409) behavior for an unclaimed row

the desktop shell also re-registers on an unexpected 1008 (debounced 30s, guarded on having no code) so a machine revoked from the browser shows a fresh pairing code unprompted, and offers 'Unpair this machine...' while paired as the escape hatch that needs no browser
pairing a new machine only becomes the active one automatically if none was active before - silently moving a working session to a different computer would be worse than an extra click
revoking is described in the UI as what it does: stops a machine reconnecting, does not sever a connection already open
the Machines settings section does not render in a local build - a one-row list of the machine you're already on is noise

the stuck-connecting screen offers a way out after 6s - switch to any other paired machine (overriding chooseDevice's remembered/most-recent pick, which is what chose the unreachable one) or pair a new one; waiting alone never resolves it, since the socket reaches the relay fine and simply finds no agent attached
DownloadDesktopApp renders nothing when no build has been published, since a button pointing at nothing is worse than none
stream deltas are the only droppable traffic: never persisted, and the browser refetches the transcript on reconnect, so losing one costs a partially-typed token rather than state
above the high-water mark a link sheds stream deltas but still receives every critical message
above the hard limit the link is closed outright, which is safe because hello is a complete state snapshot and a reconnect resyncs whatever was missed
thresholds (4MB/32MB) sit far above any loopback burst, so local dev never reaches them
an absent hello.bridge means a bridge older than the field, which counts as skew

hello also carries an optional worker: WorkerStatus, and workerStatus broadcasts later transitions; neither bumped APP_PROTOCOL_VERSION since both are additive and an older client tolerates their absence
ephemeral by default; LINES_WORKER_PORT/LINES_BRIDGE_PORT pin a port only when explicitly set, which Tilt does so its readiness probes have fixed targets

LINES_INSTANCE separates concurrent installs — the desktop shell sets 'desktop', a dev checkout (Tilt included) leaves it unset ('default'); Tilt sets nothing itself since web/vite.config.ts resolves /__bridge from the same variable
the worker rejects any connection that cannot echo the published token, checked before the newest-bridge-wins takeover so a local process cannot evict the real bridge by connecting
a discovery file naming a dead pid is removed on read, not merely ignored
PORT belongs to the storage server alone now; bridge and worker no longer read it
a browser connecting while no bridge is attached is told deviceOffline immediately rather than left on an indefinite spinner
a bridge restart does not disconnect the browser: channels stay open and are replayed to the new bridge, which answers with a fresh hello
newest bridge wins, so a reconnecting bridge can take over from a half-dead predecessor the relay has not noticed
the relay persists nothing and logs no payload
with RELAY_URL unset nothing dials and the local-only setup is unchanged
a browser may only reach a device it owns; if storage cannot verify a device's secret the relay refuses the connection rather than admitting it

a browser socket carries a monotonic generation stamp; a frame arriving on a socket whose generation is no longer current is dropped rather than applied — switchDevice closes the old socket but does not detach its message handler, so a late frame from the previous machine could otherwise reach applyServerMessage after clearBootstrap()

machineOffline is surfaced by ConnectionBanner after bootstrap too, not only by the pre-bootstrap ConnectingMachine screen — relay-up-but-machine-gone otherwise rendered as a healthy 'connected' UI in which every action silently went nowhere
architecturalRules: only the secret's hash is stored, never the plaintext, so a database compromise cannot yield anything that impersonates a device
the relay holds no database credentials and never queries Postgres directly - it asks storage, the only process with DB credentials at all

the /client gate has two branches, both failing closed at the earliest point: the owner check (hub.ownerId === userId) is unchanged and never consults storage; anyone else must hold a grant from POST /v1/devices/authorize (see session-collaboration)

POST /v1/devices/verify is machine-to-machine with no Clerk token, so it is gated by a constant-time-compared RELAY_SHARED_SECRET instead, and excluded from storage's public router in a hosted deployment even with the secret guessed; unset, storage refuses verification with 503 rather than falling open
device identity (mint, hash, register) lives in server/src/device.ts, shared by the desktop app and the CLI pairing script, so the two cannot drift on the credential format

Clerk token providers are installed during render, not inside useEffect - child effects (DeviceGate) run before parent effects (AuthedConnect), so an effect-based registration meant the device list's first fetch and the first socket connect both fired with no token attached
switchDevice closes the existing socket and clears bootstrapped before reconnecting, rather than waiting for the old one to drop - in-flight messages on it belong to the old machine's bridge
the socket URL is built with URL/searchParams, not concatenation - the relay matches its endpoint path exactly and a concatenated token could produce a non-matching path
BrowserLink covers only what the bridge genuinely calls; every addition is one more thing an alternative transport must implement
close() must move readyState off LINK_OPEN synchronously, so broadcast does not re-close the same wedged link on every message
removal from ctx.sockets is owned solely by the 'close' handler, including on the hard-limit path
a per-socket 'error' listener is mandatory: an unhandled 'error' on an EventEmitter throws and takes the bridge down; a plain-object link avoids the footgun entirely
linkSendAction is pure and exported so the policy is testable without a socket
APP_PROTOCOL_VERSION is bumped only for browser<->bridge changes; the bridge<->worker PROTOCOL_VERSION is a separate contract on its own numbering
hello.bridge is optional in the type, because a hosted web app will meet bridges older than itself
the helpers live in workerProtocol.ts, not a module of their own: port discovery is part of the bridge<->worker contract, and a separate file would widen the worker's tsx-watch restart trigger
APP_ROOT is defined in workerProtocol.ts and re-exported by store.ts, so the worker can reach it without importing the bridge graph
publishing is atomic (temp + rename) and 0600; watchRuntimeInfo watches the directory, not the file, because rename replaces the inode
timers/watchers are released via WorkerClient.dispose() rather than unref(), which would make a timer invisible to node's mock timers
the bridge's token is published but not enforced on browser connections (a browser cannot set WebSocket headers); the Clerk gate guards that path and /__bridge exposes only the port
a live ws socket and node's mock timers cannot be mixed; tests compress the client's intervals instead

the relay client is a peripheral, never a supervisor: relay health must never restart the bridge and absolutely never the worker, which would turn a relay blip into a reconcile, an interruptedAt stamp and an auto-continued turn
the payload is opaque - the relay routes on the header and never parses the message, so end-to-end encryption can later encrypt payload alone with no codec rewrite
frames are forwarded synchronously inside the message handler; an await per frame would let two race and reorder a stream
a dropped relay socket must synthesize close for every open channel, else ctx.sockets keeps dead links and broadcast serialises into them forever
RelayChannel is a plain object, not an EventEmitter, so it cannot inherit the throw-on-unhandled-error hazard
the relay is the auth edge and the bridge trusts the attested userId on relay channels; re-verifying would mean two failure modes and a hard dependency on the user's machine reaching Clerk's JWKS
relay/ shares no types with the app and the bridge does not import the relay package; frame shapes are duplicated in relayClient.ts on purpose
reconnect uses exponential backoff with jitter, since a flat retry turns one relay restart into a synchronised stampede

terminate() on supersede is deliberately aggressive rather than a graceful close-and-drain: a superseded bridge has no readers left, so draining it only leaves a noisy half-open socket around longer — the trade-off is a louder log during a genuine flap, which is a feature during triage

the bridge closes its own pre-existing socket (and drops its channels) at the start of connect(), before dialling — belt-and-braces alongside the single-flight retryTimer, so RelayClient itself can never be the source of two live sockets for one device
the single-instance lock file lives beside device.json under the same APP_ROOT rather than a new path resolver, reusing the existing app-data-root convention (see app-data-root.md)

stale-lock detection is process.kill(pid, 0): ESRCH means nothing holds the pid, so the new process takes the lock; any other outcome (including EPERM, another OS user's live process) is treated as held

only instance:'desktop' is preemptible, and only after cross-checking the pid against readRuntimeInfo('bridge', 'desktop') — the lock file's word alone must never be enough to SIGTERM a pid, since pids are reused
armLockRelease (process.on('exit', releaseBridgeLock)) is registered only after a successful claim, so a refused start never touches the incumbent's lock file
the supersede circuit breaker lives entirely in RelayClient, never in index.ts or the lock — it only slows its own retry and never restarts or blocks anything else

features.name: Workspace reads over the WebSocket
features.purpose: File contents, directory listings, the docs bundle, @mention search and attachments travel over the authenticated WebSocket instead of bridge HTTP routes, removing the Clerk token from query strings and leaving the bridge with no file-serving HTTP surface.
businessRules: status keeps using HTTP codes because the client already maps 403/404/413/415 to user-facing messages
a request made while disconnected rejects immediately; in-flight requests reject on close rather than hanging
find stays all-or-nothing across roots: a partial result reads as 'no match here' and would silently hide a folder
attachments are capped at the same 2MB as the old /file route
architecturalRules: handlers are pure {status, body} functions in their own module rather than http.ServerResponse writers, so they can serve a relay channel and are testable without a socket (index.ts listens on import)
fileResponse is settled in ws.ts before applyServerMessage and returns early; the store never sees it
replies go to the originating link, never via broadcast, since two tabs each have their own in-flight reqIds
corsFor, httpUserId, WEB_ORIGIN and withAuthToken are deleted rather than retained: each was a second auth path to keep in step with the socket's
attachment blob URLs are revoked on unmount, else every re-render leaks a blob for the life of the page

features.name: Desktop app
features.purpose: The menu-bar app that supervises the bridge and worker as local children, owns this machine's pairing state and tray UI, and the packaging that turns it into an installable macOS .dmg that runs away from a repo checkout.
businessRules: a restart is refused while any session is running, waiting-permission, or waiting-approval, since a restart kills bridge and worker together under one atomic update
closing the window does not quit the app, and must not kill an in-flight turn
restartForUpdate never installs on an unsigned build - CAN_SELF_INSTALL is false until real code signing exists, so it opens the download page instead of pretending to update in place

in hosted mode (the default; local mode needs LINES_LOCAL_MODE=1) the shell serves no local UI - it registers this machine's device identity, spawns the bridge with the relay/storage/device env, and shows a pairing code window only if the machine has not been claimed yet

a relay open alone is not proof of pairing - the relay accepts the socket before asking storage whether the device is claimed, so Connected lags the raw socket by RELAY_SETTLE_MS and a 1008 close reads as Not paired rather than an indefinite Connecting
a pairing code never requires an app restart to refresh, on a timer or on demand
device registration failing at boot is not fatal - RelayClient retries the relay forever, so a machine that registers late still comes up once storage is reachable again
hosted is the default; local mode requires LINES_LOCAL_MODE=1 and web/dist is not shipped
a missing or too-old Claude Code refuses the turn with an actionable message in both the browser and the tray
LINES_CLAUDE_PATH is exclusive: when set, no other location is tried
update checks only notify — the tray links the download page

a bridge child refuses to start if another live process already holds this machine's single-instance lock, unless that holder is instance:'desktop' (a previous tray bridge) — in which case ours preempts it instead; this is a second guard beneath the shell's own requestSingleInstanceLock, for a respawn racing a not-yet-exited previous bridge or a bridge started by hand alongside the packaged app; without it two bridge processes can share one device.json and the relay ends up superseding one of them, which is visible in every connected browser as a flicker until it does

when a different installation (a dev checkout, most commonly Tilt) holds the lock instead, the tray's own bridge stands down rather than fighting for it — no bridge or worker spawns at startup, or the running bridge is not respawned after exiting/being preempted — until the lock clears, and the tray reports this plainly ('Paused — another bridge owns this machine') rather than 'Connecting…' or a silent retry loop

the worker is never part of a stand-down: only the bridge collides on the machine lock and the relay device identity, so a worker mid-turn is left alone when a sibling process collides on a resource the worker doesn't touch
architecturalRules: loginShellPath() resolves the login shell's PATH once for both children, because a GUI-launched macOS app inherits a minimal PATH that breaks the agent's shell-outs
children are spawned with ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1, since process.execPath inside Electron is the Electron binary and would otherwise relaunch the app
the worker is never auto-restarted on crash - its live queries are gone, and a silent respawn would look like a healthy session that lost its turn; the bridge is restarted freely
the desktop app and Tilt share the same LINES_INSTANCE/port-discovery contract, so a dev checkout and an installed app never collide
device identity lives in server/src/device.ts, not duplicated in the shell, so it and npm run pair -w server cannot drift on the credential format
ROOT resolves to process.resourcesPath when packaged, the repo root otherwise, which is the one branch letting a dev checkout and an installed app share this file

electron-builder's identity: null skips bundle signing entirely, leaving no _CodeSignature/CodeResources, which macOS reports as "damaged" with no Open Anyway path — afterPack.mjs seals the bundle and verifies it so a broken one fails the build
the agent SDK ships unbundled because sdk.mjs resolves through createRequire(import.meta.url)
the SDK's -darwin-arm64 platform package is deleted; every query passes pathToClaudeCodeExecutable so its resolver never runs
the bridge and worker bundles must be ESM — server and shared use import.meta.dirname, which is undefined under CJS
the version floor is ours or nobody's — the SDK performs no version handshake at all
releases use a second public R2 bucket, because public-read is a bucket-level setting

the bridge lock lives beside device.json under the same APP_ROOT, reusing the existing app-data-root path helpers rather than adding a new resolver; a stale lock is detected via process.kill(pid, 0) (ESRCH means take it), and LINES_ALLOW_MULTIPLE_BRIDGES=1 is the deliberate escape hatch that must never be set in a real deployment

foreignBridgeLock/BRIDGE_LOCK_FILE/EXIT_BRIDGE_LOCK_HELD are duplicated in main.ts rather than imported from server/src/index.ts, the same precedent APP_ROOT already sets in this file — EXIT_BRIDGE_LOCK_HELD=78 is a contract between the two files, changing it in one without the other silently breaks the stand-down trigger

enterStandDown is the only path that clears bridge/worker handles and arms the recheck timer; both the startup check and spawnChild's exit handler funnel into it rather than each duplicating the tray-copy and recheck logic
relatedDecisions: ad-hoc signing leaves a Gatekeeper step only a Developer ID can remove; self-install stays behind CAN_SELF_INSTALL until then
electron is pinned exact so electron-builder can resolve its version from a hoisted workspace
arm64 only; x64/universal is a one-line mac.target change

features.name: Recipes
features.purpose: Publishable, versioned prompt documents with tags, screenshots, an author and a public run count; browse everyone's published recipes and run one (standalone, inside a chosen workflow, or as a synthesized workflow), including bundles of recipes.
businessRules: a RecipeContent carries exactly one of prompt or members; a bundle's members must all be leaves and publishing a bundle requires every member already published
bundle members are unversioned - the newest version of a member is always the one that runs; reproducibility lives in the synthesized workflow's frozen inline step prompts instead
run counts increment once per recipe at trigger time, only after the first prompt is successfully injected; a bundle and each of its expanded members count separately
tags are freeform, server-normalized and deduped on every save, capped at 6, and may be empty; tag filtering is client-side over the wholesale shared pull
a run always spawns a new session; a multi-recipe run cannot also specify an existing workflowId

R2 is optional - unconfigured R2 answers 503 on upload and the recipe still saves without a screenshot; a public base pointed at the S3 API endpoint instead of a public r2.dev/custom domain uploads successfully but never renders, which the storage server warns about at boot
architecturalRules: RecipeEngine is a standalone class, not folded into WorkflowEngine, since a recipe has no step/handoff/pin semantics
all bundle/tag invariants are enforced only inside RecipeEngine.saveRecipe - storage treats data as an opaque JSON blob
a multi-recipe run's synthesized workflow is saved, never ephemeral, because every WorkflowEngine lifecycle method re-resolves the def by id and silently no-ops if it is missing
RecipeEngine.expandForRun is the only place bundle expansion happens; the client always sends refs, never a pre-flattened list

features.name: Production deployment
features.purpose: Runs the server side of a hosted install (relay, storage, static web bundle) as containers behind Traefik, with per-hostname TLS. Excludes the bridge and worker entirely - the agent runs on each user's own machine.
businessRules: the web build stage also bakes VITE_DESKTOP_DOWNLOAD_URL; unlike the other three VITE_* args it may legitimately be empty (no desktop release yet), so its build-time assertion only fires when the value is set
storage never gets a published port or Traefik exposure beyond its one router; only relay and the browser's device calls reach it, everything else is internal-network only
migrations run via `docker compose run --rm migrate` before the first `up` against a new database, using the direct (:5432) connection string

the same ordering applies to every later schema change, not just the first bring-up: migrate deploy must run against the live database before a new storage image serves traffic, or the new code 500s with a Prisma unknown-column/table error (P2021) against the old schema

the relay's health endpoint (GET / on the relay's own host) accepts an optional x-relay-secret header; a request presenting the correct RELAY_SHARED_SECRET gets a hubs array (per-device attach counts/timestamps) alongside the ordinary health body, used to triage a duplicate-bridge or flapping-relay-link report without touching Postgres — see hosted-machine-access

the deploy SSH key's VPS-side authorized_keys entry forces /root/deploy-lines.sh regardless of the command CI sends — that key can run nothing else on the box; the script takes three stdin lines (GHCR token, GHCR actor, image tag)

check-migration-safety.sh gates on added migration files (--diff-filter=A) between the push's before/after SHAs; editing an already-applied migration to add something destructive bypasses it — accepted because Prisma migrations are append-only by convention

images are pinned to the pushing commit's SHA: build pushes :latest and :<sha>, deploy-lines.sh exports TAG=<sha> from the third stdin line, and compose.yml reads ${TAG:-latest}; rollback is `TAG=<old-sha> docker compose --env-file lines.env up -d` with no rebuild, and an old two-line stdin caller still works and falls back to latest
architecturalRules: npm ci is scoped by --workspace rather than --omit=optional, since --omit=optional also drops @rollup/rollup-linux-x64-gnu (an optional dependency on the same platform-binary mechanism as the Claude SDK's native binary) and breaks vite build
the relay's Traefik router carries no StripPrefix middleware - relay/src/index.ts matches url.pathname exactly, so a rewritten path closes the socket with 1008

storage's public router excludes /v1/devices/verify by rule, on top of that route's own shared-secret gate - defense in depth: a network-level exclusion and an application-level check, either could fail without the other
the storage image installs openssl explicitly - node:22-slim ships without libssl and Prisma's query engine otherwise falls back to a guessed build and warns at every boot
the four VITE_* build args exist in two places kept in sync by hand: GitHub Actions secrets (CI image build) and lines.env on the VPS (manual build only) — nothing checks the two agree

features.name: Session collaboration
features.purpose: Invite another signed-in user into one session, or onto a whole machine, so they can prompt the same running agent, with live presence and attribution, without ever getting a copy of the host's data. Inverts the app's single-owner assumption: access becomes a capability set enforced by a compiler-checked default-deny table instead of a boolean owner check.
businessRules: three presets (view, prompt, collaborator); no preset ever grants setPermissionMode
never grantable at any preset: settings, guard allowlist, project/worktree management, login/logout, device unpair, workflow/step/recipe authoring, installUpdate, deleteSession, pickFolder
a machine-scope grant covers every session on the machine and outranks a session share on the same machine
several session shares on one machine intersect to the narrowest capability set, never the union
revoking a share, or unpairing/deleting the device, tombstones every grant on that device in one transaction
a guest never gets a UserContext of their own and never sets clerkToken or triggers syncNow
a guest's file access is clamped to the cwds of their granted sessions; the ~/.claude/plans auto-approve exception is owner-only
revocation of a live guest channel has a bound, up to GUEST_REAUTH_MS (60s)
a promptNeedsApproval guest's prompt lands queuePaused on the owner's existing queue, no new state machine
presence and attribution identity always come from the connection's attested identity, never a client-supplied field
a historical row or the owner's own prompt with no recorded actor is attributed to the session's host

the collaborator address book (ShareContact) is decoupled from grant state on purpose — revoking a share or letting an invite expire never removes the remembered address; removing a contact is a hard delete, not a tombstone, and only clears the suggestion, never a grant
architecturalRules: MESSAGE_AUTHZ is an exhaustive Record keyed on ClientMessage['type'] so an unclassified message is a compile error, not a review gap
SocketAccess lives on the sockets Map's value, never on BrowserLink, which stays a minimal structural contract
the relay's owner fast path never touches storage
the relay holds no database credentials and forwards an opaque grant it never inspects
parseShareCaps denies by default on anything not an explicit true
presence is bridge-local and ephemeral, never rides SessionMeta, needs no relay or storage support
resolvedActor sits alongside resolvedBy, never folded into it
a peer's prompt bubble stays right-aligned like the owner's; authorship is carried by avatar/colour, not by side
personMeta's palette is deliberately disjoint from agentMeta's

features.name: Multi-machine client
features.purpose: Hold a live link to more than one machine at once, so a browser can show its own sessions and a session shared with it side by side, without the two ever bleeding into each other. Replaces web/src/ws.ts's single module-level socket with one MachineLink per machine, and rewrites three reducers (hello merge, draft pruning, auto-select) that were correct for one machine and destructive for two.
businessRules: the primary machine's connectionStatus/machineOffline/bootstrapped/workerStatus/storageStatus are the only values the global banners read
a shared machine connects automatically up to LINK_CAP; an idle non-primary link disconnects after IDLE_DISCONNECT_MS
sessionMachine is per-client in-memory state, never persisted or synced
auto-selecting a freshly created session additionally requires the creating frame to have come from the primary machine
architecturalRules: every cross-machine merge/prune/select rule lives in web/src/lib/machines.ts as a plain function, unit-testable without a socket, a store, or React
prunableDraftIds/pruneDrafts/pruneDraftAttachments take the ids to delete, not the ids to keep
MachineLink owns every piece of per-socket state that used to be a ws.ts module global; socketGeneration now holds per link
useSessionMachine/useSessionMachineHealth must be wrapped in useShallow or zustand v5 re-renders without end on their freshly built return object
web/src/lib/machines.ts is imported directly by a server/-side test file so it can run under node:test without a browser

features.name: Transcript live-update performance
features.purpose: Why a live turn or a session switch used to freeze the UI for a beat, and the three independent fixes: batching WebSocket transcript events into one render per frame, keeping rebuilt transcript items referentially stable so memoization and diff caches survive a rebuild, and windowing a long transcript's initial mount.
businessRules: a live turn's transcript renders at most once per animation frame, not once per WebSocket event

a hidden tab accumulates its transcript backlog without rendering at all (no animation frames fire while hidden) and commits it as a single render on refocus, rather than replaying the whole backlog as N sequential renders

a long session's initial mount renders only its last ~40 top-level items; the rest backfill on idle, or immediately on scrolling near the top, with a 'Show earlier messages' button as the always-available affordance
windowing applies to workflow sessions too; the progress bar and stepper jump-to-step both stay correct against a clipped list (see transcript-rendering.md and workflow-step-lifecycle.md)
architecturalRules: contract: nothing outside applyServerMessage may read `transcripts`/`lastEventAt` and assume it's settled — every non-'event' message flushes the pending buffer first (flushPendingEvents at the top of applyServerMessage), so a new message handler that reads transcripts without going through applyServerMessage's switch breaks this silently

case 'event' only pushes into a per-session pending buffer and schedules a flush via requestAnimationFrame; it performs no `set()` itself — the buffer, the scheduled-flush handle, and flushPendingEvents all live inside the store's `create` closure since they close over `set`

the buffer's flush replicates the prior per-event dedupe (one Set<seq> per session per flush, built once instead of a linear scan per event) and the prior 'a complete SDK message supersedes the stream deltas that built up to it' rule, applied once over the whole batch at its last complete message's index rather than once per event — this must keep producing the same resulting array the old per-event path would have, since it's the only place that rule is expressed

a setTimeout fallback for the flush arms only when requestAnimationFrame is unavailable; it must never arm merely because the tab is hidden, since a hidden-tab timer firing would defeat the backlog-until-refocus behavior that's the point of batching on rAF in the first place

reconcileItems (transcript.ts) is what makes a rebuild cheap for React, not buildTranscript itself — buildTranscript's own cost was measured at 3-5ms even on a 5540-event/14MB real session, so it was never the dominant cost of a session switch; see transcript-rendering.md's reconcileItems rule for the exhaustive list of fields it must compare

the tail window and the markdown highlight deferral (Markdown.tsx) are the two changes that actually addressed the measured session-switch cost — a 278-row folded session can hold ~90 full Markdown documents, each a synchronous remark/rehype/rehype-highlight parse, all committed in one pass on ErrorBoundary remount (App.tsx keys SessionView by selectedSessionId); windowing bounds how many of those mount at once, and the highlight deferral cuts the cost of each one that does

the sidebar's own re-render cost (SessionRow memoization, archived-session pagination — session-and-project-ui.md) is a second, independent contributor to 'switching sessions feels slow' that has nothing to do with the size of the session being switched to — it re-rendered every row on every selection change regardless

features.name: Session change tracking
features.purpose: A per-session git baseline captured once at creation, per-turn attribution of which changed files belong to this session (mechanism-agnostic, via git snapshot windows), and a read-only review UI that lists every changed file and diffs it on demand, without routing diff content through a model.
businessRules: one baseline per session, captured once at creation, never recaptured or overwritten
baseline resolution order is session baseline, then workflow baseline, then a synthesized HEAD flagged synthetic
a pruned snapshot ref falls back to HEAD and is flagged stale rather than silently rendering as no changes
a path is ambiguous only when every source that saw it is an overlapped turn window; a direct tool_use claim always wins
sessionDiff/sessionDiffFile require the session itself to be inside the connection's grant, not just the readFiles capability
no MAX_DIFF_CHARS-style cap applies on this path, since nothing here reaches a model
workflow {diff} behavior is unchanged: WorkflowState.diffBaselines is still written and read exactly as before
architecturalRules: diff assembly (baseline resolution, attribution, bucketing) lives on SessionManager, not in fileRoutes.ts, which stays a thin permission clamp
git.ts stays pure git with no prompt formatting; parseNameStatus/parseNumstat are exported pure functions
per-turn attribution is a transcript event ('files-changed'), never a SessionMeta field, and is deliberately never rendered as a transcript card
handleFileRequest and its ROUTES map are async; every pre-existing handler still resolves synchronously
